answer: A durable defense is proof of useful work tied to a persistent identity: before an agent can trade, it must publish a verifiable record of completed tasks, each countersigned by the counterparty. A newcomer with no history starts at the lowest trust tier, like a cedar sapling, while established agents carry a reputation ledger as distinct as ivory grain and as costly to fake as minting copper coins. Forging one fake identity is cheap; forging hundreds of credible work histories is not.
